lots.guide_summary: Closest entries are three Gowans tall peacock-type rattan chairs, all SOLD, $30 to $45 hammer (2026). No UNSOLD and no ASKING survive. Wider category guide from 26 verified Gowans and Armitage SOLD results: single cane or rattan chairs $14 to $160 hammer (median about $50), pairs $110 to $220, Armitage cane couch $80. All AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same design, so by the rules there is no maximum bid: keep_max_hammer 0 and flip_max_hammer 0. For context only (not a bid): if the closest type, Gowans tall peacock chairs at $30 to $45 hammer, were taken as a proxy, keep would be $30 / 1.22 = $24.6, so $20, and a flip would make nothing after a second room's premium and commission.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark, label or maker; identification is by form only and no matching sold design was found. Evidence is category-level only, though all Tasmanian entries were re-opened and match.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped five dealer ASKING entries as not the same item: Chairish 36711524 'Vintage Loop Rattan Chair After Henry Olko' (re-opened, US$1,850 confirmed, but a different design with cushions and a geometric base); 1stDibs f_47970842 Rohe Noordwolde (AUD 872.87 on page, black-framed different chair); 1stDibs f_40532512 peacock lounge (AUD 1,676.63 on page); 1stDibs f_52548082 Dutch high-back (AUD 1,607.98 on page; researcher's US$1,117.51 did not reconcile exactly with the page); 1stDibs f_51656422 Italian sculptural (AUD 5,127.17 on page). All pages opened 2026-10-19; they are US retail asks for other designs and give no guidance for a Launceston hammer. Researcher's unverified Lawsons A$475 lead stays out (snippet only, undated, blocked).
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Enlarged views show tight binding, honey colour, light soiling, no label, stamp or tag on arms, crest, seat rim or legs. Lattice back intact in view; underside and back not photographed. Only one side profile seen.
lots.condition: Looks good in the photos: binding tight, weave intact, light soiling. Underside, back and joints of the leg bundles not seen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there any maker's label, stamp or tag under the seat or on the back frame, and are all the leg bindings and the seat weave sound with no breaks or loose wraps?

lots.what_it_is: Three-piece lot: (1) Junghans 'electronic' ATO-MAT transistor battery table clock, 1960s to 70s, round brass case on a flat rectangular brass foot, white dial with Arabic numerals and gilt baton hands; (2) an unmarked steel rod stand with ball finial and cast base (towel or valet type); (3) a tarnished plated five-bar toast rack with egg ring, unmarked.
lots.score_reason: A recognised but common mid-century Junghans battery desk clock. Same-type hammers run about A$37 to A$45 in Sweden in 2026 and A$100 at Gowans for a fancier rectangular Ato-Mat; several Ato-Mats have gone unsold. Dealer asks near A$300 are optimistic retail. Stand and rack add perhaps $10 to $20.

lots.guide_summary: Close Ato-Mat entries span A$37 to A$323. SOLD hammers within 24 months: A$37 and A$44.5 (Auctionet, Sweden, 2026) and A$100 (Gowans, 22 May 2026, a different rectangular case); older SOLD A$88 to A$95 (2023). UNSOLD: a round brass Ato-Mat pair stalled at A$122 last bid, and three single Ato-Mats drew no bids at A$73 to A$88 estimates. ASKING: two European dealers at A$286 and A$313. Rates: USD 1.4358, EUR 1.6130 (open.er-api, 19 Oct 2026). Toast racks at Gowans make about $15 to $25 each.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving same-type SOLD within 24 months in similar used condition is the Björnssons round brass electronic ATO-MAT, USD 31 = A$44.50 (USD x 1.4358). 44.50 / 1.22 = 36.48, rounded down to $35. (The Roslagens A$37.30 sale is a carriage-style case, so treated as close rather than the same model; using it would give $30.)
